rationale: B shows consistent, context-linked shifts and varied engagement: it responds to TOUCH (t=8), CALL by orienting to PERSON_ALPHA (t=20–23), OFFER_FOOD by moving to the TROUGH (t=32–41), PRESENT_OBJECT by focusing on PLAY_BALL for many ticks (t=44–65), and STARTLE by leaning away with a prolonged, graded recovery (t=68–77). It also initiates sensible, spontaneous shifts (e.g., to PLAY_CHIME at t=30–31, to PERSON_BETA at t=66–67) and even vocalizes toward a person (t=42–43). A reacts to TOUCH, OFFER_FOOD, and STARTLE but ignores CALL (t=20) and PRESENT_OBJECT (t=44), and spends long stretches with attention NONE (t=40–67, 72–95), indicating lower autonomy and adaptability.
